headline: Penguins place Sam Girard on injured reserve
take:
Daily Faceoff reports the Penguins have placed Sam Girard on injured reserve, noting he last appeared in the lineup on Oct. 17 against the Golden Knights. Nothing in the report says how long he will be out or what the injury is.

The Penguins are 4-6-1 for 9 points through 11 games, and the numbers suggest the record is not telling the whole story. Their share of expected goals (the quality of chances they create versus allow) is 48.7 percent overall, a touch under even, but at five-on-five it rises to 53 percent. That means the underlying play at even strength has been solid so far this season. The weaker spots are special teams: PIT creates 0.47 expected goals per game on the power play and allows 0.7 per game on the penalty kill, both modest figures. Goaltending has also helped, with PIT's goalies saving 1.5 goals above expected. Girard's absence matters most if the lineup change leans on those special-teams units, though we have no data yet on who will absorb his minutes, so any shift in ice time remains unclear.
